title: Bounded allowable-torsion derived theorem
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be smooth and $g:T\to S$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and let $Y=X\times_ST$ with projections $h:Y\to X$ and $e:Y\to T$ be the base-change square of [sbc-def-base-change-square]. Let $\mathcal P$ be the set of primes invertible on $S$. For every $K\in D^b_{\mathcal P\text{-tor}}(T_{\Et})$ [sbc-def-derived-categories-with-allowable-torsion], the exchange map of [sbc-def-base-change-map], with abelian-sheaf coefficients,
$$\operatorname{BC}_{f,g}(K):f^{-1}Rg_*K\longrightarrow Rh_*e^{-1}K,$$
is an isomorphism in the ambient derived category of abelian sheaves on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. If both its source and target are bounded, they belong to $D^b_{\mathcal P\text{-tor}}(X_{\Et})$, and this map is an isomorphism in that full subcategory as well.

proof.text:
Choose integers $a\leq b$ such that $\mathcal H^q(K)=0$ outside $[a,b]$, as allowed by [sbc-def-derived-categories-with-allowable-torsion]. Apply [def-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-filtrations] to the square with its notation $(f,f',g,g')$ replaced by our $(g,h,f,e)$: the source scheme is $T$, the base is $S$, the changed base is $X$, and the changed source is $Y$. This gives convergent spectral sequences on $X$ with finite filtrations on each abutment,
$$E_{2,A}^{p,q}=f^{-1}R^pg_*\mathcal H^q(K)\Longrightarrow\mathcal H^{p+q}(f^{-1}Rg_*K),\qquad E_{2,B}^{p,q}=R^ph_*e^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K)\Longrightarrow\mathcal H^{p+q}(Rh_*e^{-1}K).$$
Only $p\geq0$ and $a\leq q\leq b$ can contribute. The exchange morphism is the one in [sbc-def-base-change-map]. The assertion (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-couple-morphism] gives a morphism of exact couples, hence the comparison of these sequences; assertion (3) identifies its $E_2^{p,q}$ map with the degree-$p$ base-change map on $\mathcal H^q(K)$. Thus the comparison is induced by the specified map, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism between the abutments.

source.place: Proof, hypercohomology comparison; exact-couple compatibility made explicit

proof.text: For each $q$, the stalk condition in [sbc-def-derived-categories-with-allowable-torsion] says that every element of every geometric stalk of $\mathcal H^q(K)$ is killed by a positive integer all of whose prime divisors lie in $\mathcal P$. Each of these primes is invertible on $S$, so that integer, being a product of powers of invertible primes, is invertible on $S$. The hypotheses of [sbc-thm-smooth-base-change] therefore hold for $\mathcal H^q(K)$: $f$ is smooth and $g$ is qcqs. It makes each comparison $f^{-1}R^pg_*\mathcal H^q(K)\to R^ph_*e^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K)$ an isomorphism for $p\geq0$; the terms for $p<0$ are both zero. Hence every $E_2$ comparison of step 1 is an isomorphism.

source.place: Proof, apply smooth base change to each cohomology sheaf

proof.text: The vanishing outside $[a,b]$ and the $E_2$ isomorphisms of step 2 are exactly the hypotheses of [sbc-lem-finite-range-comparison]. It gives isomorphisms on all the abutments and, in particular, says that $\operatorname{BC}_{f,g}(K)$ itself is an isomorphism. Because step 1 identifies the comparison with this exchange map, this proves the ambient derived-category assertion. No boundedness of the two outputs is required: the finite interval is the interval of cohomology of $K$, not a cohomological-dimension bound for $g$ or $h$.

source.place: Proof, finite-range comparison and ambient conclusion

proof.text: We verify the allowable-torsion condition on the outputs, which boundedness alone does not imply. Apply [lem-sbc-qcqs-higher-images-prime-torsion] to $g:T\to S$ and to each $\mathcal H^q(K)$, using the input condition of [sbc-def-derived-categories-with-allowable-torsion]. Thus all $R^pg_*\mathcal H^q(K)$ have $\mathcal P$-torsion stalks. By [lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar], pulling these sheaves back along $f$ preserves this condition. The first spectral sequence of step 1 therefore has $\mathcal P$-torsion stalks on $E_2$. Each successive page is a kernel modulo an image, so all its stalks, and those of $E_\infty$, have the same condition: subgroups and quotient groups inherit annihilators. By [def-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-filtrations] the abutment in each degree has a finite filtration with these $E_\infty$ terms as successive quotients. Apply the exact stalk functor of [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] to this filtration. For an extension $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$ of such groups and $x\in B$, choose an allowed integer $n$ killing its image in $C$ and an allowed integer $m$ killing $nx\in A$; then $mnx=0$, and the prime divisors of $mn$ still lie in $\mathcal P$. Induction through the finite filtration shows that every $\mathcal H^n(f^{-1}Rg_*K)$ has $\mathcal P$-torsion stalks. The isomorphism of step 3 transfers this condition to $\mathcal H^n(Rh_*e^{-1}K)$ as well.

source.place: Proof, bounded allowable-torsion conclusion; the omitted torsion verification

proof.text: If both outputs are bounded, step 4 and the definition in [sbc-def-derived-categories-with-allowable-torsion] put both in $D^b_{\mathcal P\text{-tor}}(X_{\Et})$. This is a full subcategory of the ambient derived category, so the exchange map and its inverse from step 3 are morphisms in this subcategory, with the same inverse identities. This proves the bounded-category assertion.

source.place: Proof, restriction of the ambient isomorphism to the full bounded subcategory
